title: Sales Representatives of Services, Except Advertising, Insurance, Financial Services, and Travel

tasks.short: Answer questions about service options, prices, availability and agreed credit terms.

steps.what: Receive the question and clarify the service, account and requested date.

loop.input: Written customer question or seller-entered summary of a live question.
loop.output: Question category, service reference, account reference, requested date and missing fields.
loop.check: Validate references against permitted records; preserve the original question and flag ambiguity.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt; unresolved identity or meaning returns to the seller.
loop.why_not_simpler: Written requests use varied language; structured forms cover only part of the intake.

steps.what: Find the relevant service description and approved answers.
Look up the current price and any agreed account discount.
Check service capacity and available delivery dates.
Check the account's approved payment and credit terms.
Explain the relevant options, price, availability and approved terms.

loop.input: Question brief and permission-filtered service, price, availability and credit facts.
loop.output: A concise answer with internal citations and explicit gaps.
loop.check: Prices, dates and terms must match source fields exactly; the seller approves before use.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing, stale or conflicting facts require a human answer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover standard questions; combined questions need short explanations adapted to the customer's wording.

steps.what: Discuss unusual requirements and refer requests for changed terms.

tasks.design: A {WORKFLOW} intake identifies the question, then retrieves approved service facts from the {DOCS}, prices from the {CRM}, capacity from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and existing credit terms from the {ERP}. Exact lookups and calculations run as rules; a bounded model drafts combined explanations with internal citations. The seller approves customer-facing answers, while changed prices, capacity commitments or credit terms follow existing approval routes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Answers require several lookups, and approved documents are often poorly indexed. Maintaining those joins and answer templates has required scarce implementation time.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing search, structured lookups and access controls handle the factual work. AI-assisted coding can make a small answer desk economical, with a model used only for intake and wording.
tasks.still_hard: Availability can change between lookup and commitment. Missing account terms and unusual requirements still need an authorised person.
tasks.human_edge: Notice what the customer is really asking and explain trade-offs without making unsupported promises.
tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time searching and more time on unusual requirements and buying concerns. No new pricing, capacity or credit decision rights are assumed.

reach.task: Check account details and explain already approved payment terms.
reach.learn: Account identity checks, confidentiality boundaries and when finance approval is required.

evidence.claim: Approved-document answers with citations and deterministic price lookups are feasible building blocks.
The Air Canada case documents liability for incorrect chatbot information, supporting strict controls on customer-facing factual claims.
Article 50 requires disclosure for direct AI interaction unless it is obvious; it matters if a customer-facing AI channel is later introduced.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates.
Service guidance, price books and approved account terms have identifiable owners.
Availability is informational until a separate booking or service commitment is confirmed.
The solution reads existing credit terms; it does not score creditworthiness or decide new terms.
Live calls remain with the seller; no new call recording is assumed.
GDPR applies to account data. Access and any employee consultation required under national rules are included in the estimate.
An initial version can use authorised exports with visible freshness dates.
unknowns: Where do authoritative prices, account discounts and capacity records reside?
How current must each answer be before the seller can use it?
What proportion of questions arrive in writing versus live conversation?
Who approves exceptional prices, delivery promises and credit terms?
Which access and employee consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Which question categories can use exact approved answer blocks without a model?
Can the source systems expose freshness and account-level permissions reliably?
How much review time remains for combined questions during live calls?
new_work: Maintain service guidance, answer categories and price-source mappings.
Review generated wording before customer use.
Resolve missing terms, stale availability and conflicting source facts.
Sample answers for incorrect commitments and unnecessary disclosure of account data.
tasks.statement: Answer customers' questions about services, prices, availability, or credit terms.

tasks.short: Learn from industry events and publications, then apply relevant developments to sales work.

steps.what: Review industry publication and event listings in an industry information service.
Coordinate event attendance through {EMAIL} and add arrangements to the {CALENDAR}.
Read selected publications and identify developments relevant to services and customers.

loop.input: Selected publications and explicit learning questions.
loop.output: A reading guide with cited developments, quotations and sections worth reading in full.
loop.check: Verify that references resolve; the seller checks important claims and reads the relevant originals.
loop.stop: One guide and one repair per publication; inaccessible or uncertain material returns to manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keyword alerts locate material but cannot reliably explain its relevance across varied prose.

steps.what: Attend the trade event, ask questions and discuss developments with participants.
Write a learning brief linking event observations and publications to account questions.

loop.input: Seller-written event notes, verified reading notes and permitted account context.
loop.output: A learning brief separating sourced facts, participant opinions and questions to investigate.
loop.check: Preserve source references and attribution; the seller checks meaning and removes confidential material.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unclear notes remain questions rather than asserted facts.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template organises the brief, but connecting varied notes needs bounded synthesis.

steps.what: Discuss the learning brief with colleagues and agree useful follow-up questions.

tasks.design: Configure publication alerts and a learning shortlist, with attendance arrangements handled through the {WORKFLOW} and {CALENDAR} after seller approval. Bounded loops prepare cited reading guides and draft learning briefs in the {DOCS} from selected publications and seller-written notes. The seller attends events, reads important originals and agrees follow-up questions with colleagues.
tasks.previous_blocker: Event value depended on live conversations, while preparation and follow-up were fragmented. Summaries often lost attribution or required almost as much checking as manual notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing alerts and calendar workflows handle coordination. Source-linked reading guides and bounded drafting reduce preparation without assuming that a summary replaces learning.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected conversations and tacit industry knowledge cannot be scheduled or reliably summarised. Regulatory interpretation may require a qualified internal specialist.
tasks.human_edge: The seller asks follow-up questions, notices disagreement and develops relationships that make later conversations more candid.

ambition.what: A monthly sector-change briefing for the account team.

tasks.altitude: The seller keeps substantial time for attendance and learning, with less coordination and note preparation. They gain responsibility for proposing account discovery questions; regulatory approval authority does not change.

reach.task: Turn industry learning into team development priorities.
reach.learn: Facilitation, evidence quality and how to test whether a briefing changes customer conversations.

reach.task: Assess whether an industry innovation changes service feasibility.
reach.learn: Technical dependencies, implementation constraints and how to frame questions for specialist review.

evidence.claim: Publication alerts, attendance workflows and source-linked reading guides can reduce supporting work while attendance remains human.
The digest provides no documented outcome for replacing industry-event attendance or professional learning.
Build ranges and remaining-time percentages are planning estimates.

assumptions: The time split describes a typical mix over several weeks; some weeks involve only reading.
Existing publication alerts and calendar features are available.
Paid attendance requires the existing budget approval before any registration action.
Publication reuse follows access and licensing terms.
The design uses seller-written notes and introduces no participant recording or employee scoring.
GDPR applies to personal information in notes. Applicable EU AI Act duties and national employee consultation rules depend on deployment.
unknowns: Which publications are licensed for automated processing?
What is the actual mix of reading, online meetings and physical events?
Who approves attendance spending and external registration?
Which event notes may be shared internally?
Does the rollout require employee consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Do reading guides help sellers identify the original passages that matter?
Which event formats produce useful follow-up relationships or account questions?
Can the monthly briefing produce specific customer questions without duplicating the market brief?
new_work: Curate publication alerts and remove low-value sources.
Check citations, attribution and confidential details in learning briefs.
Maintain attendance approval rules and calendar connections.
Review whether briefings improve account preparation.
tasks.statement: Attend sales or trade meetings or read related publications to obtain information about market conditions, business trends, regulations, or industry developments.

tasks.short: Calculate service costs, compare options and explain the trade-offs to customers.

steps.what: Read the service request and clarify quantities, scope and delivery assumptions through {EMAIL}.

loop.input: Service request and relevant account context.
loop.output: Draft costing assumptions with missing fields and source quotations.
loop.check: Validate required fields, units and quantities; the seller resolves ambiguities before calculation.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair; missing scope returns to the seller for customer clarification.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requests arrive in varied prose; structured requests can bypass the loop.

steps.what: Retrieve current rates, supplier costs and existing contract terms from the {ERP} and {DOCS}.
Calculate service options, recurring charges and one-off costs in a {SPREADSHEET}.
Assess service differences, exclusions and uncertainty before choosing suitable options.
Prepare the customer comparison document and save its assumptions against the {CRM} opportunity.
Explain the comparison to the customer and answer questions about the options.

tasks.design: A rate-card app on the {WORKFLOW} retrieves approved rates from the {ERP} and contract fields from the {DOCS}, using versioned formulas to compare service options. A bounded loop drafts assumptions from incoming {EMAIL}; missing or conflicting terms stop the calculation for seller review. Templates generate the customer comparison and save its costing record in the {CRM} after approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rates, contract conditions and customer scope were spread across systems. Small differences in units or exclusions made copied calculations unreliable.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding reduces the effort of building rate imports, validation and document templates. The model only extracts request details; formulas calculate all amounts.
tasks.still_hard: Bespoke delivery effort, uncertain volumes and negotiated terms can dominate the result. Missing cost ownership must be resolved before reliable automation.
tasks.human_edge: The seller understands which trade-offs the customer will accept and when a cheaper option would fail their needs.

ambition.what: Compare package economics during each substantive scope revision.

tasks.altitude: The seller spends more of the week exploring viable service combinations with customers. They can recommend alternatives using current economics; no additional discount or contract authority is assumed.

reach.task: Check whether proposed service configurations are deliverable.
reach.learn: Capacity constraints, effort estimation, service dependencies and the difference between price and delivery cost.
Required order fields, billing schedules and how scope changes affect fulfilment.

evidence.claim: Rule-based rate cards, calculation engines and templates can support service comparisons without model arithmetic.
Salesforce Agentforce for Revenue supports quote creation from a typed sentence; this is adjacent capability, not proof of cost-comparison accuracy.
Salesforce reports 75% less quoting time and 87% fewer clicks for its own sales team; the digest gives no base or period.
Build ranges and remaining-time percentages are planning estimates for this design.

assumptions: Internal delivery costs and customer-facing prices remain separate fields with separate access controls.
Rates have owners, effective dates, units and an explicit tax basis.
Deterministic rules block expired rates, missing inputs and incompatible units.
Contract terms are supplied as approved structured fields; ambiguous clauses require a person.
Use existing {CRM} calculation and template features first if they cover the required rules.
GDPR controls apply to customer data; applicable EU AI Act duties and national consultation rules must be addressed.
Build estimates cover a limited service catalogue and exclude a full pricing-system replacement.
unknowns: Does the {CRM} already support the required calculations and comparison templates?
Which system owns authoritative rates and delivery costs?
How many service families, currencies and tax treatments are in scope?
Who may approve customer-facing comparisons and exceptional terms?
What access and employee consultation are required for the deployment?
research_questions: Can historical comparisons be reproduced from versioned rates and assumptions?
Which exceptions require commercial judgement rather than another calculation rule?
Does the comparison expose all material exclusions and recurring commitments?
new_work: Maintain rate versions, formulas and service dependencies.
Resolve missing scope, stale rates and conflicting contract terms.
Review customer-facing comparisons before release.
Check calculation changes against representative historical cases.
tasks.statement: Compute and compare costs of services.

tasks.short: Help clients resolve problems and use the service after signing.

steps.what: Discuss the problem, its impact and the client's desired outcome.
Find account history, service records and earlier support cases.
Check the agreement and service guidance for applicable remedies.

loop.input: Issue brief, relevant agreement sections and approved service guidance.
loop.output: Applicable obligations, possible remedies and unresolved questions, with source passages.
loop.check: Verify account access, document versions and citations; the seller checks applicability.
loop.stop: One retrieval pass and one revision; missing or conflicting terms go to the contract owner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Client descriptions and agreement wording vary; exact field matching misses relevant obligations.

steps.what: Discuss remedies and agree a proposed resolution with the client.
Approve remedies outside the seller's delegated limits.
Assign the agreed service fix and chase the responsible team.
Record the resolution, owner and next follow-up date.
Send the client a written resolution and progress update.

tasks.design: Join account history in the {CRM}, cases in the {HELPDESK} and agreement references in the {CLM} into one case view. A bounded reading step prepares a cited remedy brief; the seller handles the conversation and approval limits route exceptions through the {WORKFLOW}. Approved resolutions create service work orders, update the {CRM} and prepare client updates in the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Account history, contract terms and delivery updates sit in separate places. Linking them and maintaining reliable handoffs often cost more than the perceived saving.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing case routing and approval features cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce connector effort, while a bounded reading loop handles varied issue descriptions.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed obligations, delivery failures and damaged trust need context and negotiation. Source records can also disagree.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise the client's real concern, repair trust and choose a proportionate remedy.

ambition.what: Weekly decisions on recurring service failures across the seller's accounts.

tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time finding records and chasing updates, and more time resolving difficult cases. A weekly failure review becomes feasible; authority to grant remedies still follows delegated limits.

reach.task: Review recurring account problems and prioritise service improvements.
reach.learn: Separate isolated complaints from repeated failures and estimate account impact.

evidence.claim: Case joins, routing, reminders and structured record updates can use deterministic integration and workflow rules.
A cited reading assistant can prepare remedy options, but applicability and relationship repair remain human judgements.
The Air Canada case illustrates the consequences of incorrect automated service information; it does not establish outcomes for this occupation.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates, not measured results.
The baseline is an established service business with account records and a support process.
Exceptional approvals are averaged across cases; routine remedies use existing delegated limits.
A first version can use authorised exports and approved documents before write access is available.
GDPR applies to client data. National rules determine employee consultation requirements; access and applicable consultation are included in the estimate.
Build ranges cover one service line and working days; consultation can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which system holds authoritative service status and account identifiers?
What remedies can the seller approve, and who approves exceptions?
Are agreements searchable and linked to the correct account?
Which access permissions and employee consultation arrangements apply?
research_questions: Can account and case records be joined reliably without broadening access?
How often do approved remedies require interpretation beyond the available guidance?
new_work: Review cited remedy briefs and resolve conflicting documents.
Handle failed handoffs, overdue fixes and client updates requiring sensitive wording.
Maintain approval limits, document versions and account-to-case mappings.
Review recurring failure patterns with service delivery.
tasks.statement: Consult with clients after sales or contract signings to resolve problems and provide ongoing support.

tasks.short: Contact customers to understand their needs and discuss suitable services.

steps.what: Review account history, open opportunities and outstanding service issues.
Arrange a discussion with the customer.
Discuss needs, explain service options and agree next steps.
Write customer notes from the discussion.

loop.input: Seller-entered discovery bullets and agreed next steps.
loop.output: Customer notes separating stated needs, commitments and unresolved questions.
loop.check: The seller checks commitments and names against the original bullets before saving.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; missing or disputed facts return to the seller.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text discovery findings vary; a fixed template alone cannot condense them reliably.

steps.what: Create follow-up tasks with owners and deadlines.

tasks.design: Configure an account brief in the {CRM}, linked to the {HELPDESK}, and scheduling through the {CALENDAR} for customers who have agreed to a discussion. A bounded loop turns seller-entered bullets into reviewed customer notes; structured next steps create tasks in the {CRM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Account context crossed systems, and discovery findings remained free text. The conversation itself depends on trust and changing customer needs.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing views and scheduling can be configured cheaply. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting records and adding a small, checked drafting loop.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding unstated needs and recovering strained relationships remain human work. Contact permission, GDPR processing grounds and national outreach rules must be reflected in scheduling eligibility.
tasks.human_edge: Earn trust, notice hesitation and help customers express needs they have not yet articulated.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of accounts needing a new discovery conversation.

tasks.altitude: Preparation and paperwork take less of the week, leaving more time for discovery. The seller gains better evidence for choosing which accounts to revisit; formal decision rights do not change automatically.

reach.task: Translate discovery findings into a feasible service scope.
reach.learn: Learn service constraints, acceptance criteria and when technical discovery is needed.

evidence.claim: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales supports lead research and qualification, demonstrating account preparation capabilities.
Configured account views, scheduling and structured follow-up tasks need no autonomous agent.
Preparation can shrink while relationship-led discovery remains human; time estimates are planning assumptions.

assumptions: The company uses a {CRM} and has an approved service catalogue.
Automatic scheduling is restricted to customer-requested or already-agreed discussions.
Notes use seller-entered bullets; call recording is not required.
Step shares describe a typical contact cycle and are not measured customer data.
Build ranges cover a starter implementation; access and consultation can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Whether account and service-ticket records share reliable identifiers.
Which contact permissions and processing grounds are recorded.
Which account fields the seller may access.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed changes.
research_questions: Which account facts actually change the seller's preparation?
Can existing scheduling configuration handle customer booking and cancellation?
Which discovery-note fields require explicit seller confirmation?
new_work: Review drafted customer notes and commitments.
Handle scheduling exceptions and incorrect account links.
Maintain brief fields, access rules and note templates.
Complete employee consultation under national rules where applicable.
tasks.statement: Contact prospective or existing customers to discuss how services can meet their needs.

tasks.short: Prepare sales forms and agreements from accepted commercial terms.

steps.what: Confirm the accepted offer, contracting entity and intended start date.
Collect customer, billing and signatory details.
Select the approved agreement template and required schedules.
Populate the agreement with the accepted scope, prices and terms.
Review and approve requested departures from standard clauses.
Approve the commercial agreement for issue.
Prepare the signature request and send the approved agreement.
Check signature status and remind outstanding signatories.
File the signed agreement and update the opportunity and service handover.

tasks.design: Populate approved templates in the {CLM} from accepted offer data in the {CRM} and billing details in the {ERP}, using fixed template and clause rules. The {WORKFLOW} routes departures and commercial approvals, then sends only the approved document version through the {ESIGN}. Signature events update the {CLM} and {CRM} and produce the service handover; no model is needed for the standard path.
tasks.previous_blocker: Offer data, agreement templates and signature requests are disconnected. Template variation and unclear data ownership make seemingly simple copying difficult to automate reliably.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing template, approval and signature features can handle the standard path. AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of field mapping, validation and event handling without changing legal judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Nonstandard liability, ambiguous scope and signatory authority remain difficult. A signed agreement must match the approved version exactly.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise a material departure from the deal and negotiate obligations the organisation can honour.
tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time copying fields, arranging signatures and filing agreements. No new authority to change clauses, accept risk or approve commercial terms is assumed.

reach.task: Validate the contract-to-service handover before service setup.
reach.learn: Mandatory order fields, billing dependencies and checks that prevent premature service activation.

evidence.claim: Teamleader provides customer records and quotes that can be signed online; its Focus AI acts after approval.
Template population, approval routing, signature reminders and signed-document filing can run deterministically.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates.
The accepted offer has structured scope, price and term fields; otherwise the seller must first confirm them.
Templates and clause rules are approved and versioned.
Legal review applies only to departures; standard agreements bypass that branch.
The signature step cannot alter the approved document or recipient list without renewed approval.
Reminder frequency is capped, and disputes or changed recipients return to the seller.
GDPR applies to contact and signatory data. National rules determine any employee consultation requirements, included alongside access in the estimate.
Build ranges cover one agreement family; authorised exports can support draft generation before write access is available.
unknowns: Which agreement templates and clause-selection rules are approved?
How complete and reliable are accepted-offer fields?
Who can approve commercial terms, legal departures and signatory details?
Which signature events and document certificates are available?
What access and employee consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Can the accepted offer populate every mandatory agreement field without interpretation?
Can the signature request be bound to the exact approved document version?
Can repeated signature events be processed without duplicate records or service handovers?
new_work: Maintain field mappings, templates and clause-selection rules.
Resolve missing details, signatory changes and nonstandard clauses.
Handle declined signatures, expired requests and failed synchronisation.
Check that approved, signed and archived document versions remain linked.
tasks.statement: Create forms or agreements to complete sales.

tasks.short: Prepare tailored sales presentations and proposals that explain the service.

steps.what: Confirm the client's objectives, requirements and buying concerns.
Collect account details and relevant opportunity notes.
Select service descriptions, specifications and approved examples.
Calculate the proposed service scope, quantities and indicative price.
Write and assemble the tailored proposal or presentation.

loop.input: Proposal brief, approved source pack, priced scope and fixed section structure.
loop.output: Tailored narrative inserted into a proposal or presentation template.
loop.check: Trace factual claims to approved sources; verify all prices and specifications against structured inputs.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported requirements remain visibly unresolved for the seller.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates fill facts, but explaining how the service meets varied client objectives needs tailored prose.

steps.what: Check unusual specifications and delivery claims.
Approve the final proposal and send it to the client.

tasks.design: A proposal generator takes an approved brief from the {CRM}, selects tagged material from the {DOCS} and calculates scope and prices with deterministic rules. A bounded model writes the tailored explanation into fixed templates, with claims linked to their sources. Specialist checks and the seller's final approval precede sending through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful material is scattered across old proposals, and each seller repeats document assembly. A maintained template and pricing integration has often been too expensive for smaller service lines.
tasks.enabler_now: Template rendering, document tagging and pricing rules already work without models. AI-assisted coding lowers assembly costs, and a bounded drafting loop reduces rewriting.
tasks.still_hard: Poor discovery produces a polished but irrelevant proposal. Bespoke delivery promises and claims about outcomes still require expert judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Choose the argument that matters to this buyer and recognise requirements the service cannot honestly meet.

ambition.what: Smaller accounts needing a tailored service proposal.

tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time assembling documents and can prepare tailored proposals for smaller opportunities. The seller gains room to choose which opportunities deserve tailoring; commercial approval limits still apply.

reach.task: Translate client requirements into a feasible service scope.
reach.learn: Service dependencies, exclusions and evidence needed to support delivery claims.

evidence.claim: Approved templates, deterministic pricing and bounded narrative drafting can be combined into a proposal generator.
Salesforce Agentforce for Revenue supports generating quotes from a typed request; this supports the quoting component, not the full proposed presentation workflow.
Salesforce reports 75% less quoting time in its own sales team, with no base or period given; this is not a forecast for this design.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates.
This baseline uses a maintained rate workbook where formal quoting is not fully configured in the {CRM}.
Existing quoting and template features should be configured first where they meet the need.
Approved material can be tagged by service and client need without a model.
Specialist review applies to unusual scope; its time share is averaged across proposals.
GDPR applies to client briefs. Confidential examples require permission for reuse.
Build estimates include access and applicable employee consultation under national rules; no seller scoring is introduced.
The first version covers one service family and can use authorised exports.
unknowns: Are prices governed in the {CRM}, a rate workbook or another authorised source?
Which examples and claims are approved for external reuse?
Which specifications require specialist approval?
Which smaller opportunities currently receive only generic proposals?
What access and consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: How much tailoring can approved conditional sections handle before a model is useful?
Can every factual claim in a sample proposal be traced to a current approved source?
Does the generated document remain readable across the required output formats?
new_work: Maintain templates, service tags, pricing rules and approved examples.
Review tailored narratives for relevance and unsupported claims.
Resolve gaps between requested and deliverable scope.
Check rendered documents after template changes.
tasks.statement: Develop sales presentations or proposals to explain service specifications.

tasks.short: Give relevant promotional materials to people at meetings and events.

steps.what: Select current, approved promotional materials from the {DOCS}.
Coordinate quantities, printing and delivery with the marketing coordinator.
Check and pack printed materials for the event.
Offer attendees relevant materials and briefly explain their purpose.
Email requested digital materials to attendees who supplied their contact details.

tasks.design: Approved collections in the {DOCS} populate event packs, and a configured {WORKFLOW} sends internal preparation requests using agreed quantity rules. An attendee can request a specific digital item through a form, triggering its approved link through {EMAIL}. Packing, choosing what to offer and the event conversation remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: The task is mostly physical and interpersonal; small administrative savings rarely justified a separate build.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document collections, forms and notification rules can cover preparation and requested delivery with little custom code.
tasks.still_hard: Physical packing, event logistics and judging when an attendee welcomes an approach.
tasks.human_edge: Reading interest, choosing a relevant item and making a useful personal introduction.
tasks.altitude: Event days remain largely unchanged, with less coordination and follow-up email. No new decision rights are gained.

reach.task: Prepare audience-specific demonstration and information kits.
reach.learn: Approved service examples, accessible formats and matching materials to audience needs.

evidence.claim: Approved document collections, internal forms and requested-link delivery can be configured without a model.
Physical distribution and attendee interaction limit the overall time saving.
No digest case establishes a measured improvement for event-material distribution.

assumptions: Printed distribution remains useful; digital delivery is an attendee choice.
Preparation requests stay within preauthorised quantities and do not place supplier orders.
Approved materials have current versions and audience or language tags.
Automatic delivery sends only the item explicitly requested to the supplied address.
A material request does not enrol an attendee in broader marketing.
GDPR and applicable national marketing rules govern contact capture and retention. Access estimates include any required employee consultation.
unknowns: Whether events use printed materials, digital materials or both.
Who currently handles printing and physical preparation.
Existing document tags, approved collections and request forms.
Typical event volumes and administrative effort.
Applicable contact-retention rules and national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Can existing {DOCS} and {WORKFLOW} configuration cover the entire administrative portion?
Which materials do attendees request often enough to justify a dedicated digital collection?
new_work: Keep event collections and approved links current.
Handle incorrect addresses and failed deliveries.
Maintain quantity defaults and event preparation rules.
Remove expired contact requests according to retention rules.
tasks.statement: Distribute promotional materials at meetings, conferences, or trade shows.

tasks.short: Recommend service features that match customer needs and delivery capabilities.

steps.what: Review account history and earlier requirements in the {CRM}.
Explore customer needs, priorities, constraints and acceptable trade-offs.
Check service descriptions, exclusions and delivery limits in approved documents.
Compare relevant features and prepare reasons for recommending each option.

loop.input: Confirmed customer requirements, rule-filtered services and approved capability descriptions.
loop.output: A comparison linking features and limitations to stated needs, with source references.
loop.check: Every service must pass eligibility rules; every capability claim needs an approved source; the seller reviews trade-offs.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; unsupported capabilities or conflicting requirements return to the seller.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle layout, but linking conversational needs to feature explanations requires contextual writing.

steps.what: Recommend features, explain limitations and test the customer's understanding.
Record the recommendation and agreed next action in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: A configured account view in the {CRM} provides history, while deterministic filters retrieve suitable services and their limitations from approved information in {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop prepares a sourced comparison for the seller's conversation. The seller makes the recommendation and confirms structured requirements and next actions in the {CRM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Service knowledge was spread across documents, and recommendations depended on interpreting each customer's priorities.
tasks.enabler_now: Searchable capability records and inexpensive comparison generators reduce preparation without requiring automated recommendations.
tasks.still_hard: Discovering unstated needs, checking unusual delivery promises and balancing conflicting customer priorities.
tasks.human_edge: Eliciting priorities, challenging assumptions and accepting responsibility for the recommendation.

ambition.what: A documented service-fit review before renewal

tasks.altitude: The seller's week still centres on discovery and recommendation conversations, with shorter preparation and recording. They can propose service-fit reviews; authority to promise exceptions remains unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare an initial feasibility brief for unusual service requirements.
reach.learn: Capability boundaries, requirement traceability and when specialist validation is needed.

evidence.claim: Rules can filter service options, while sourced drafting can reduce comparison preparation; the recommendation remains human.
Existing sales software supports customer records and approval-controlled assistance, but this does not establish recommendation quality.
Most conversation time remains because discovery and trade-off judgement dominate this task.

assumptions: The pilot covers ordinary services outside the excluded advertising, insurance, financial and travel categories.
Core eligibility constraints can be represented as structured fields or maintained rules.
The deterministic search shows source passages; it does not infer undocumented capabilities.
The seller enters customer responses through a short structured form; no recording or transcription is required.
The proposed renewal review is an ambition, not an existing customer service.
GDPR applies to account information and customer notes. Access planning includes consultation required by national rules.
unknowns: Completeness and ownership of the service catalogue and delivery constraints.
Which promises require service-delivery or commercial approval.
How often requirements involve exceptions or bespoke services.
Whether customers would value a separate service-fit review.
Existing permissions and applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which eligibility checks can be encoded without hiding important exceptions?
Can comparison drafts preserve limitations as reliably as benefits?
What minimum requirements make an initial feasibility brief useful to a sales engineer?
new_work: Maintain capability fields, exclusions and source versions.
Review comparisons for missing limitations and unsupported benefits.
Escalate uncertain feasibility to service specialists.
Confirm structured records after conversations.
Evaluate whether proposed service-fit reviews improve customer decisions.
tasks.statement: Emphasize or recommend service features based on knowledge of customers' needs and vendor capabilities and limitations.

tasks.short: Find prospective service customers from directories, referrals and events.

steps.what: Review territory, target criteria and existing accounts in the {CRM}.
Search business directories and collect relevant business details.
Discuss introductions and potential needs with clients or event contacts.
Combine leads in a {SPREADSHEET} and check existing records in the {CRM}.
Assess business fit and choose leads worth pursuing.

loop.input: Deduplicated lead records, source excerpts, referral notes and approved target criteria.
loop.output: Suggested fit category, supporting excerpts and unresolved questions for each lead.
loop.check: Validate required fields and source references; the seller confirms the shortlist.
loop.stop: One classification and one repair attempt per lead; incomplete or unsupported cases return to the seller.
loop.why_not_simpler: Industry and size filters are rules; referral language and service needs require contextual interpretation.

steps.what: Create or update lead records and assign the next action in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: Approved directory feeds enter the {CRM} through a deterministic integration that checks identifiers and existing accounts, removing the separate {SPREADSHEET}. A bounded model loop interprets referral notes and proposes a sourced shortlist for seller review. Configured {CRM} rules assign approved leads and next actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Directory access, inconsistent identifiers and referral notes made a reliable import expensive to maintain.
tasks.enabler_now: Integration code is cheaper to build, while a bounded classification loop can handle free-text referrals.
tasks.still_hard: Directory licences, stale contacts, ambiguous account matches and introductions that depend on personal trust.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising a credible introduction and judging whether a service need is real.

ambition.what: Daily selection of the next prospect cohort within the assigned territory

tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time assembling lists and more time testing prospect groups and developing introductions. They can reprioritise within their assigned territory; budget and territory rights need explicit delegation.

reach.task: Compare prospect cohorts and recommend changes to territory priorities.
reach.learn: Conversion analysis, sample size limits and selection bias.

evidence.claim: Lead research and fit assessment are supported by an existing sales qualification product.
Feed imports, duplicate checks and routing can use deterministic rules; referral interpretation can use a bounded loop.
The proposed time reductions and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.

assumptions: The pilot covers one sales team, one {CRM} and approved directory sources.
The business directory is the OTHER category in step s2 and provides a licensed feed or export.
Referral discussions remain human; the solution does not contact prospects.
The {CRM} becomes the shared lead register, replacing the intermediate {SPREADSHEET}.
GDPR applies to identifiable contacts. Access planning includes lawful sourcing, retention and consultation required by national rules.
unknowns: Available directory licences, feeds and export rights.
Actual lead volumes, duplicate rates and contact-data quality.
Whether the team currently maintains a separate lead workbook.
Approved target criteria and the seller's delegated prioritisation rights.
Applicable national rules and employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which available directory interfaces provide stable business identifiers and permitted reuse?
Can a sample of referral notes be classified accurately using the existing target criteria?
new_work: Review suggested fit categories and uncertain account matches.
Resolve failed imports and stale contact records.
Maintain source permissions, target criteria and duplicate rules.
Sample rejected leads to detect missed prospect groups.
tasks.statement: Identify prospective customers using business directories, leads from clients, or information from conferences or trade shows.

tasks.short: Explain purchased service terms, contractual obligations and practical next steps to customers.

steps.what: Find the customer's signed contract and service record.
Read applicable clauses and identify dates, obligations and service limits.

loop.input: Authoritative signed contract, amendments, service record and the customer's question.
loop.output: Relevant obligations, dates and limits with clause references and explicit uncertainties.
loop.check: Check document version, source references and date formats; the seller verifies material facts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt; conflicting clauses or missing amendments go to the seller.
loop.why_not_simpler: Negotiated clauses and amendments cannot all be mapped reliably from fixed fields.

steps.what: Compose the customer explanation using approved wording.
Check recipient, terms and attachments, then send the explanation.
Discuss questions, explain consequences and resolve misunderstandings with the customer.
Log correspondence and follow-up actions in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: A deterministic link joins the account in the {CRM} to authoritative contracts in the {CLM} and {DOCS}. A bounded extraction loop prepares cited facts for review, then configured templates produce the explanation in {EMAIL}; the seller approves each personalised send. Correspondence and confirmed follow-up actions are logged in the {CRM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Signed versions, amendments and service details were scattered, making reliable explanations depend on manual reading.
tasks.enabler_now: Document retrieval, source-linked extraction and template generation can now be combined at a practical implementation cost.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting amendments, disputed meanings and explaining unwelcome obligations without damaging trust.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding the customer's concern and explaining consequences without making unsupported promises.
tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time locating clauses and composing routine explanations. More time goes to difficult conversations; contractual authority does not change.

reach.task: Check that service handover instructions match the accepted contract.
reach.learn: Order fields, contract precedence and operational acceptance criteria.

evidence.claim: An existing product combines customer records, quotes and online signing with approval-controlled AI actions.
Source-linked contract extraction and template generation are feasible design patterns; this workflow has no documented outcome in the digest.
A documented chatbot case illustrates the consequences of sending incorrect contractual information.
Time reductions and build ranges are estimates requiring a local pilot.

assumptions: The pilot covers one service family and a limited set of explanation templates.
Signed contracts and amendments have identifiable authoritative versions.
Configured templates cover routine explanations; unusual wording returns to the seller.
The workflow explains existing terms and does not amend contracts.
Logging uses sent messages and seller-confirmed notes, without introducing call recording.
GDPR requires account-level access and appropriate retention. Access estimates include consultation required by national rules.
unknowns: Where authoritative signed versions and amendments are stored.
Which explanations require legal or service-delivery approval.
Whether contractual notice channels differ from ordinary customer email.
Existing document permissions, retention rules and integration access.
Applicable national consultation requirements and approval lead times.
research_questions: Can the retrieval process consistently identify the controlling contract and amendments?
Which common questions can be answered entirely through approved templates?
new_work: Verify extracted facts and approve personalised sends.
Resolve conflicting versions and ambiguous obligations.
Maintain templates, clause mappings and document permissions.
Sample explanations for unsupported statements and omitted limitations.
Route contractual disputes to the authorised role.
tasks.statement: Inform customers of contracts or other information pertaining to purchased services.

tasks.short: Maintain accurate customer and account records in connected systems.

steps.what: Collect approved customer changes and agreement details from source records.
Find the correct customer record and check for duplicates.
Update customer fields, account status and agreement references.
Copy approved billing changes into the customer finance record.
Update the parallel account tracker and reconcile copied fields.
Clarify conflicting details and resolve ambiguous customer matches.

tasks.design: Deterministic integrations collect approved structured changes from the {CRM}, {ERP} and {ESIGN}, match stable identifiers and update only permitted fields with an audit log on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Ambiguous matches enter an exception queue in the {WORKFLOW}; shared views in the {CRM} replace the parallel tracker in the {SPREADSHEET}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Systems lacked consistent identifiers and field ownership, so sellers copied changes and kept a parallel tracker. Exception handling made integrations appear broader than they needed to be.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of adapters, validation and retry handling. Existing matching, permissions and shared views can cover much of the work.
tasks.still_hard: Legacy duplicates, conflicting field ownership and restricted interfaces remain expensive. GDPR requires appropriate access, retention and processing grounds for customer data.
tasks.human_edge: Know when two records represent different buying relationships and verify changes that affect the customer.
tasks.altitude: Routine copying and tracker reconciliation largely leave the seller's week. They retain exception verification and gain time for customers; no new commercial decision rights arise from record automation.

reach.task: Validate new customer details before account activation.
reach.learn: Learn legal-entity identifiers, required account fields and the boundary between contact edits and sensitive finance changes.

evidence.claim: Teamleader provides customer records and online quote signing, showing that linked commercial records are available today.
Structured record updates, identifier matching and synchronisation can use deterministic integrations without a model.
A parallel tracker can be eliminated when its necessary fields and views exist in the authoritative system.

assumptions: Most updates come from structured, approved source fields, consistent with the task priors.
Free-text-only changes enter the human exception path rather than being guessed.
Automatic writes exclude bank details, new credit decisions and destructive record merges.
Billing changes have already received any required finance approval.
The parallel tracker contains copied fields rather than a distinct planning process.
Time shares and build ranges describe a starter design, not measured results.
unknowns: Which fields have authoritative owners across the {CRM} and {ERP}.
Whether stable customer identifiers exist and how many duplicates remain.
Whether signed agreement metadata is available as structured fields.
Whether the parallel tracker contains unique information.
Which write permissions, retention rules and national consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Which source events can trigger updates without seller re-entry?
Can existing synchronisation configuration handle the permitted fields?
Which mismatches must block a write rather than generate a warning?
What prevents retiring the parallel tracker?
new_work: Resolve ambiguous identities and conflicting source values.
Monitor failed writes, retries and integration credentials.
Maintain field mappings, validation and retention rules.
Review access permissions and complete national employee consultation where applicable.
Verify that shared views cover the retired tracker's useful functions.
tasks.statement: Maintain customer records using automated systems.

tasks.short: Track market changes and competitors, then decide which developments matter for accounts.

steps.what: Review competitor websites and market intelligence feeds for service and price changes.

loop.input: Changed pages from approved public sources and previous market observations.
loop.output: Dated service and price changes with source links, quotations and uncertainty flags.
loop.check: Validate dates, currencies and source references; a seller checks material claims against quotations.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per page; unreadable or ambiguous pages enter a manual queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Page changes are detected deterministically, but relevant terms appear in varied prose.

steps.what: Check recent wins, losses and customer objections in the {CRM}.
Discuss changing needs and competitor experiences with customers and colleagues.
Combine observations in a {SPREADSHEET} and compare like-for-like service terms.
Decide which changes warrant account follow-up or escalation.
Write and share a short market brief through {EMAIL} or {CHAT}.

loop.input: Verified market comparison and the seller's market priorities.
loop.output: A short brief linking each factual claim to its source.
loop.check: Reject unsupported figures and missing references; the seller approves the wording and audience.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved claims are omitted or returned to the seller.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply structure, but explaining varied developments needs limited prose synthesis.

tasks.design: A scheduled job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} detects changes in approved public sources and combines them with permitted {CRM} exports. A bounded extraction loop supplies cited observations to a {BI} comparison, while the seller adds conversation notes and chooses priorities. A drafting loop prepares the market brief for approval before distribution through {EMAIL} or {CHAT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources used inconsistent service descriptions, and internal evidence sat apart from public information. Maintaining connectors and comparable terms cost more than occasional manual research.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding reduces the effort of building collectors, change detection and comparison views. Bounded extraction can handle prose while preserving quotations for checking.
tasks.still_hard: Competitor prices may exclude important conditions. Customer anecdotes are selective, and interpreting a change still needs commercial context.
tasks.human_edge: Customers reveal concerns through trusted conversations. The seller distinguishes a meaningful competitive shift from noise.
tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time collecting and formatting evidence and more time testing its meaning with customers. They choose account follow-up priorities; changes to company pricing still require the existing commercial mandate.

reach.task: Prepare evidence for territory and segment reviews.
reach.learn: Sampling bias, win-loss definitions and how to distinguish account signals from wider market changes.

evidence.claim: Scheduled collection, structured comparisons and cited summaries are feasible building blocks; this design's savings are unmeasured.
The supplied time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not observed customer measurements.

assumptions: Start with a small public-source list; permitted exports can substitute for direct integrations.
Structured comparison rules flag unmatched units, contract lengths and missing conditions instead of forcing equivalence.
Conversation notes remain seller-written; recording and seller scoring are outside this design.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties apply. Employee consultation follows national rules where required.
Build ranges cover a limited pilot after scope agreement; consultation and source licensing may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which public sources may be collected and reused?
Are structured loss reasons and customer objections available in the {CRM}?
Which customer information may enter the shared comparison?
What access approvals and employee consultation does the deployment require?
research_questions: Which sources provide enough context to compare services fairly?
How often do verified market alerts lead to a useful account action?
What proportion of source changes can be extracted without manual correction?
new_work: Review material extracted claims and ambiguous comparisons.
Maintain source permissions, connectors and service-term mappings.
Remove stale observations and monitor missing or broken sources.
Check that briefs distinguish evidence from commercial interpretation.
tasks.statement: Monitor market conditions, innovations, and competitors' services, prices, and sales.

tasks.short: Negotiate service prices and agreement terms with customers.

steps.what: Review the opportunity, current quote and existing agreement.
Calculate concession options and their margin effects.
Negotiate scope, price, timing and reciprocal commitments.
Request approval for concessions outside delegated limits.
Approve, reject or revise exceptional commercial terms.
Prepare revised terms from the authorised commercial position.
Check revised terms and send the commercial response.

tasks.design: A small scenario calculator joins approved costs and rate cards to the opportunity in the {CRM}, while the {WORKFLOW} routes concessions beyond delegated limits. Templates in the {CLM} generate revised terms from structured, authorised choices, and the seller approves the response before the {EMAIL} sends it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Costs, concession limits and agreements were scattered, making each negotiation pack expensive to assemble. Bargaining itself cannot be reduced to discount rules.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes a narrow calculator and approval integration cheaper to build. Existing templates and approval features handle the routine parts without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Service costs can be uncertain, and nonstandard clauses require specialist judgement. Commercial authority and agreement versions must stay aligned.
tasks.human_edge: Read the customer's priorities, trade concessions for reciprocal value and know when to walk away.

ambition.what: Same-day selection among scope, price and payment-term trade-offs.

tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time reconstructing economics and chasing approvals. Within existing delegated limits, they can compare and choose concession packages during the conversation; wider authority requires an explicit management decision.

reach.task: Evaluate concession requests against margin and account value.
reach.learn: Learn contribution margin, approval thresholds and how reciprocal commitments affect deal quality.

evidence.claim: Rate-card calculations and approval limits can be implemented with deterministic rules.
Teamleader provides commercial records and online quote signing, supporting the feasibility of connected agreement workflows.
Negotiation remains human while calculations, routing and templated responses can shrink.

assumptions: Most proposed changes use approved commercial options and clauses.
The seller records negotiated choices as structured fields.
Exception approvals are conditional; step shares average standard and exceptional negotiations.
Custom legal wording goes to a legal reviewer outside the standard template path.
Build ranges assume one service family and an existing approval policy.
unknowns: Whether current cost data supports useful margin calculations.
Who may approve discounts, payment changes and contractual exceptions.
Whether the {CLM} supports field-driven templates and version control.
Which access reviews or employee consultation national rules require.
research_questions: Which concessions recur often enough to encode as options?
Which cost uncertainties should appear as ranges in scenarios?
Can existing approval configuration replace approval requests in the {EMAIL}?
new_work: Maintain cost inputs, concession limits and approved clauses.
Review exceptional commercial packages and nonstandard wording.
Check that generated terms reflect authorised choices.
Monitor failed approval routing and outdated agreement versions.
tasks.statement: Negotiate prices or terms of sales or service agreements.

tasks.short: Quote service prices, approved credit terms, contract terms and delivery dates.

steps.what: Read the customer request and identify required service details.

loop.input: Customer request and the approved service catalogue.
loop.output: Structured service, quantity, location, scope and requested-date fields with source references.
loop.check: Validate types and catalogue identifiers; the seller confirms scope and unsupported interpretations.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair; missing required fields return to the seller for clarification.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requests arrive as varied free text; deterministic parsing cannot reliably identify the intended service scope.

steps.what: Retrieve account terms, approved rates and applicable contract clauses.
Check available service capacity against the requested delivery date.
Confirm delivery commitments that exceed standard capacity rules.
Calculate service charges, discounts and applicable taxes.
Approve or reject pricing exceptions outside delegated limits.
Assemble the quote using approved prices, terms and dates.
Check the quote and send it to the customer.

tasks.design: A bounded loop extracts requests from the {EMAIL}; deterministic code joins rates and approved account terms from the {CRM} and {ERP} with capacity from the {OPS_SYSTEM}. The {WORKFLOW} routes commercial and delivery exceptions, then a template produces the quote using approved clauses from the {CLM}; the seller approves its release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests were inconsistent, and pricing, credit terms and capacity came from separate sources. Bespoke integrations cost more than the repetitive quoting justified.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes narrow integrations and rate calculators cheaper. Bounded extraction handles request wording while code retains control of prices and terms.
tasks.still_hard: Bespoke scope, stale capacity and incomplete cost data can invalidate a quote. New credit decisions and nonstandard legal terms remain separate authorised processes.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve ambiguous scope and explain which service commitments matter to the customer.

ambition.what: Small customers needing same-day standard service quotes.

tasks.altitude: The seller handles more standard requests with less calculation and document assembly. They can choose among approved service configurations immediately; pricing exceptions and delivery overrides keep their existing approvers.

reach.task: Convert an accepted service quote into an accurate service order.
reach.learn: Learn order-ready scope fields, delivery dependencies and how to prevent quote-to-order mismatches.

evidence.claim: Salesforce Agentforce for Revenue can build quotes from a typed request.
Salesforce reports 75% less quoting time and 87% fewer clicks for its own sales team; the digest gives no base or period.
Deterministic rate calculations, templates and bounded request extraction support the proposed design; case results do not establish its savings.

assumptions: The starter covers a service family with explicit rates and approved clauses.
Credit terms are retrieved from existing approvals; no consumer creditworthiness is scored.
Standard dates follow authorised capacity rules; exceptional commitments require operations approval.
Approval-step shares average standard and exceptional quotes.
Where existing {CRM} configuration supports the calculation, configure it before building code.
GDPR applies to customer data; employee consultation follows national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Whether rate cards, tax rules and account terms have authoritative versions.
Whether capacity checks can reserve availability or require a freshness check before release.
Which quoting functions already exist in the {CRM}.
Who approves payment-term changes and nonstandard contract clauses.
Which access and consultation processes apply to the proposed implementation.
research_questions: What proportion of requests fit the standard service catalogue?
Which pricing and date errors cause the most rework?
Can configured quote templates and approval rules replace custom components?
Which request fields need clarification before any calculation starts?
new_work: Review extracted scope and approve quote release.
Handle missing requirements, pricing exceptions and capacity conflicts.
Maintain rate cards, taxes, clause versions and approval limits.
Monitor integration failures and stale capacity data.
Check generated quote lines against approved calculations after rule changes.
tasks.statement: Quote prices, credit terms, contract terms, or fulfillment dates for services.

role_batches.altitude: The week shifts from record searches, document assembly and chasing to discovery, difficult client conversations and service follow-through. Better preparation supports judgement, while pricing, credit and contractual authority remain explicitly delegated.
reach: Sales manager: turn repeated account problems into prioritised service improvements.
Sales engineer: translate client requirements into feasible, evidenced service scope.
Order clerk: validate complete, consistent service handovers.
New accounts clerk: check account details and explain approved payment terms.
skills_to_grow: Structured client discovery and concise requirements capture.
Service scoping, exclusions and evidence for commercial claims.
Reading approval limits and recognising contractual departures.
Checking source freshness, citations and account permissions.
Diagnosing workflow exceptions and maintaining reusable templates.
role_batches.ambitious_version: A seller who can offer tailored proposals to smaller accounts and bring a weekly, evidence-based view of recurring service failures to the sales manager, while keeping sensitive commitments with authorised people.

role_batches.altitude: The seller's week shifts toward discovery, negotiation and resolving customer ambiguity. Better preparation and faster quotes support decisions within existing commercial limits; expanded authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Sales engineer: turn discovery findings into feasible service scope.
Sales manager: compare concession economics and reciprocal commitments.
Order clerk: ensure accepted quotes contain order-ready information.
New accounts clerk: validate customer identity and account details.
skills_to_grow: Discovery interviewing and service scoping.
Margin analysis and concession trade-offs.
Reading capacity constraints and delivery dependencies.
Checking model drafts against source facts.
Customer data quality, field ownership and GDPR-aware handling.
role_batches.ambitious_version: A service seller who helps customers shape feasible options, compares commercial trade-offs during discussions and serves smaller accounts with prompt standard quotes, supported by reusable calculators, templates and integrations.

role_batches.altitude: The sales representative spends less time assembling prospect lists, finding contract facts and preparing comparisons. Discovery, recommendations and relationship conversations remain central; broader commercial authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Sales manager: compare prospect cohorts and recommend territory priorities.
Sales engineer: prepare initial service-feasibility briefs.
Order clerk: verify that handover instructions match accepted terms.
Demonstrator and product promoter: assemble audience-specific information kits.
skills_to_grow: Maintain clear target criteria and interpret conversion evidence.
Check source-backed contract facts and capability claims.
Conduct discovery and explain service trade-offs.
Recognise feasibility exceptions and escalate them early.
Manage contact permissions and useful structured account records.
role_batches.ambitious_version: A consultative seller who tests prospect cohorts frequently and offers documented service-fit reviews before renewal, supported by reliable account and capability information.

role_batches.altitude: The week shifts from collecting evidence and calculating figures towards customer discovery, service trade-offs and informed account action. New decision rights centre on account priorities and learning questions; pricing, spending and regulatory authority require explicit delegation.
reach: Support sales managers with evidence for segment reviews and team learning.
Work with sales engineers on feasible service configurations.
Give order clerks complete scope and billing assumptions.
skills_to_grow: Source checking and commercially fair comparisons.
Service economics, units and sensitivity analysis.
Customer discovery and trade-off conversations.
Structured scope capture and exception handling.
Briefing colleagues with clear evidence and open questions.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Become a sector-informed account adviser who connects market developments to customer needs, tests viable service options quickly and turns field learning into useful team decisions.
